sections.heading: FAQs About Roof Cleaning in West Orange and Essex County

faqs.q: Does pressure washing damage a West Orange roof?

runs.v: Yes. Per ARMA, pressure-washing an asphalt shingle roof causes granule loss and premature roof failure, so Newark Quality Roofing uses the ARMA 50:50 wash and a low-pressure rinse.

faqs.q: Why does my West Orange roof grow moss on north-facing slopes?

runs.v: Reservation shade keeps those slopes damp, and damp slopes grow moss faster, per CSSB and NRCA guidance; moss then lifts and curls shingle edges, per ARMA.

faqs.q: Do zinc or copper strips prevent roof moss and algae?

runs.v: Zinc and copper inhibit algae growth, per ARMA and Atlas Roofing, but ARMA does not recommend adding strips to an existing roof; Newark Quality Roofing reserves them for a replacement.

faqs.q: How often does a West Orange roof need cleaning?

runs.v: The NRCA recommends an inspection at least twice a year, spring and fall, and after major storms. Roof cleaning is commonly recommended every 2–3 years in Essex County, sooner on shaded slopes.

faqs.q: How much does roof cleaning and moss removal cost in West Orange, NJ?

runs.v: Roof cleaning costs $300–$1,050, an average of $675 for a 1,500-square-foot home, per This Old House; moss prevention adds $150–$250.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to have gutters cleaned in New Jersey?

runs.v: Many roof cleaners also offer gutter cleaning, and comprehensive services include clearing debris and flushing downspouts. It is usually priced by gutter length, stories, and debris, so a tall house under reservation trees costs more; no matter the house, get a written price first.

faqs.q: How much does a roof inspection cost in New Jersey?

runs.v: Newark Quality Roofing provides free roof inspections across the West Orange area, so the check before a cleaning costs nothing; paid inspections elsewhere vary with roof size and height.

faqs.q: What is the average lifespan of a roof in New Jersey?

runs.v: Asphalt shingle roofs typically last about 20–30 years in New Jersey; slate lasts 60–150 years and metal 40–80 years, per InterNACHI. Moss left in place shortens that span.
